summary: The admitted punishment-chain meal reached eat.c:eatspecial, where JavaScript passed an undeclared random variable to the existing unpunish helper. Forwarding eatspecial's operation environment fixes the caller; the complete 274-step recording now matches.

mismatch.message: ReferenceError: random is not defined in eatspecial at js/eat.js:4156

source.branch: Upstream eat.c:eatspecial (2414-2486) calls unpunish() for the punishment ball and chain. The chain branch then deliberately skips useup(); the helper removes the chain and restores the ball to the floor.
source.javascript: js/eat.js:eatspecial had the corresponding calls but passed `{ ...env, random }` where no random binding exists. js/read.js:unpunish already constructs its default RNG operations and merges rawEnv.random, so the correct caller forwards env unchanged.
callers: eat.c:doeat_nonfood -> eatspecial; cmd.c:rhack dispatches #eat to doeat
dependencies: read.c:unpunish is already implemented in js/read.js and owns its default RNG wiring; no new callee port is required.
source.resolution: Call unpunish(state, env) in both the uball and uchain branches, preserving caller-supplied random operations while allowing unpunish to supply its source default.

evidence: The baseline v70 admission evaluation reports 0/274 matched screens for v70-eat-ball-scout1. A bounded scan after admission stopped with ReferenceError: random is not defined at eatspecial (js/eat.js:4156:35).

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/eat.c:eatspecial (2414-2486) calls unpunish() when otmp equals uball or uchain, and preserves the chain by skipping useup() in the uchain branch. read.c:unpunish (3066-3077) owns the punishment removal; its JavaScript port initializes the RNG defaults itself and overlays rawEnv.random.

After changing both JS caller sites to unpunish(state, env), the bounded scan emitted and matched all 274/274 screens, RNG calls, cursors, and the input boundary in segment 0. No unported markers remain in the result.
